experiment.steer: S015 §113 a learned performance model; §27 retune on material change

model.reason: kernel autotuning, no ML model involved

headline: THE MODEL FAILED THE ONLY QUESTION THAT MATTERED, AND THEN THE PROBE SHOWED IT WAS THE DATA THAT WAS WRONG. Trained on 14 flat variants it predicted the held-out cliff at a 0.34% penalty against an actual 16.88% -- 14.15% error, NOT ranked last. Adding ONE measurement from the cliff region takes that to 2.78% and ranks it last. A performance model interpolates a landscape it has sampled; it cannot discover a cliff outside the sampled region.
why_this_landscape_makes_the_question_sh: the forge re-verdict measured the top cluster FLAT -- best 9 of 15 span 0.65% against ~4.5% arm noise -- and found the whole 20.19% spread driven by ONE configuration. On a flat landscape a model that predicts within 0.65% is not accurate, it is predicting a constant, and so is `predict the mean`. THE ONLY THING WORTH PREDICTING IS THE CLIFF, so the grader keeps the two questions apart; averaging them would let 14 easy points hide the failure on the one that decides.

prediction_written_before_the_run.flat: model will NOT meaningfully beat the mean baseline; both inside arm noise
prediction_written_before_the_run.cliff: direction right (ranked slower than every flat point), MAGNITUDE undershot
prediction_written_before_the_run.falsifier: if the cliff is not ranked last the model has no actionable content

prediction_verdict.flat: CONFIRMED and vacuous as predicted -- model 1.13% median error against the mean baseline's 1.68%, BOTH far inside 4.5% arm noise, so `beats the baseline` is not evidence of anything
prediction_verdict.cliff: WRONG IN BOTH HALVES. I predicted direction right, magnitude undershot. The direction was not right either: predicted penalty 0.34% against an actual 16.88%, and the cliff was NOT ranked slower than every flat point. MY OWN FALSIFIER FIRED -- 'if the cliff is not ranked last the model has no actionable content on this landscape' -- and it is recorded as fired.

grade.means: a model that beats the mean on the flat points by less than arm noise has NOT been shown to predict anything; the cliff row is the one that decides whether the model can avoid a bad configuration unmeasured

then_the_failure_was_diagnosed_rather_th.the_question: MODELLING failure or DATA failure? tg64_ept1 has 64 elements per threadgroup; the next smallest sampled points are 128 (tg64_ept2, tg128_ept1) and BOTH ARE FAST, so the training data contains NO GRADIENT pointing at the cliff.
then_the_failure_was_diagnosed_rather_th.the_test: measure BELOW the grid: tg32_ept1 (per_tg 32) and tg32_ept2 (per_tg 64), 200 reps each, correctness checked before timing
then_the_failure_was_diagnosed_rather_th.prediction_A_confirmed: the cliff is an OCCUPANCY THRESHOLD in elements per threadgroup: 32 -> 0.9559 ms, 64 -> 0.5954, 128 -> 0.512, >=256 -> 0.511-0.522
then_the_failure_was_diagnosed_rather_th.the_sharpest_evidence_is_a_collapse: tg32_ept2 and tg64_ept1 have DIFFERENT threadgroup sizes and DIFFERENT elements per thread but the SAME per_tg of 64, and they measure 0.5954 and 0.5955 -- agreeing to 0.02%. Two configurations that differ in both parameters landing on the same time is much stronger than a correlation: per_tg is the controlling variable and the feature bet was right.
then_the_failure_was_diagnosed_rather_th.reproducibility_check: tg64_ept1 re-measured here at 0.6002 ms against 0.5955 recorded on a different day, 0.8% apart

retraining_with_one_cliff_sample.reading: adding tg32_ept2 (per_tg 64, the SAME as the target) gives 2.78% error and ranks the cliff last -- but that is INTERPOLATION AT A KNOWN POINT, not discovery. Adding tg32_ept1 (per_tg 32) still ranks it last but OVERSHOOTS by 13.37%, because the true relationship is STEEPER THAN LINEAR in 1/per_tg: the step 32->64 costs 0.361 ms while 64->128 costs 0.083, so a linear term captures the DIRECTION and not the CURVATURE.
retraining_with_one_cliff_sample.the_actionable_conclusion: the model becomes useful exactly once one sample from the cliff region exists -- which is the measurement autotuning would have made anyway. On THIS landscape a learned performance model does not replace search; it would only compress a search that has already been run once.

what_this_licenses_in_the_forge.change: kernel_forge's THREADGROUP_PRIOR stops at 64, and that exclusion is now MEASURED rather than assumed -- the comment records the cliff shape
what_this_licenses_in_the_forge.not_changed: tg32 is NOT added to the prior. A prior's job is to skip known-bad configurations, and adding measured-bad points to it would be backwards. What changed is that tg64_ept1's badness is no longer an unexplained outlier but the visible edge of a measured occupancy cliff.
what_this_licenses_in_the_forge.champion_unaffected: every tg32 variant is slower than every point in the top cluster, so no champion anywhere moves

claim_boundary.one_primitive: a fused mul->relu->silu chain at 2^24 f32, MEMORY BOUND. A compute-bound or shape-sensitive primitive could have a landscape with real structure to learn, and nothing here says otherwise.
claim_boundary.smallest_model_that_answers_the_question: ridge on 4 features over 15 points. NOT a neural cost model, not Bayesian, no uncertainty estimates. 15 points does not support more, and a model with more parameters than the landscape has structure would be fitting the noise the forge spent 200 reps per candidate measuring.
claim_boundary.arm_quality: the new tg32_ept2 and tg64_ept1 arms carry 7.99% and 8.04% IQR, inside the 10% gate but noticeably above the flat cluster's ~4.5%; the 0.02% agreement between them is far inside both.
claim_boundary.still_not_built: §113's model in the sense of something that GENERALISES across primitives, shapes or machines. This one is fit per-landscape.
